So another observation: a week ago somebody asked the question, is there a cyclic group of order n for every n?
好的，我们开始上课。: 再讲一个观察。一周前有人问过：对每个 n，是否都存在一个 n 阶循环群？

And we gave an example of a subgroup of S_n, the symmetric group on n letters, which was cyclic of order n: it's just this sort of cycle that goes 1 to 2, 2 to 3, up to n, which goes back to 1.
好的，我们开始上课。: 我们当时在 Sₙ（n 个字母上的对称群）里找到了一个例子：循环置换 1 → 2 → 3 → … → n → 1，它是一个 n 阶循环群。

Well, here's another nice construction of such a group: Z/nZ is also cyclic of order n.
好的，我们开始上课。: 这里还有一个构造这种群的好办法：Z/nZ 也是 n 阶循环群。

And it's a nice sort of model for a cyclic group of order n. Remember, we saw that all cyclic groups of order n are isomorphic.
好的，我们开始上课。: 它是 n 阶循环群的一个很好的模型——记得我们见过，所有 n 阶循环群都同构。

So here is a very simple sort of way of studying cyclic groups of order n.
好的，我们开始上课。: 于是我们就有了研究 n 阶循环群的简单办法。

Of course, this is just generated by 1-bar, because if I add 1-bar to itself k times, then this thing is just k-bar, so I get all of 1-bar, 2-bar, up to (n − 1)-bar, and n-bar, which is just 0-bar.
好的，我们开始上课。: 当然，它由 1-bar 生成：把 1-bar 自加 k 次就得到 k-bar，于是我们得到 1-bar, 2-bar, …，(n − 1)-bar，还有 n-bar，而 n-bar = 0-bar。

So why — the question is: why is the cyclic group generated by 1-bar all of Z/nZ?
好的，我们开始上课。: 那么为什么——问题是：为什么由 1-bar 生成的循环群就是整个 Z/nZ？

Well, what is the cyclic group? It's the set of — in one notation, the powers — but in our notation this is sort of inappropriate. We don't want powers, we want multiples.
好的，我们开始上课。: 什么是循环群？用某种记号说，它是幂的集合；但在我们的记号里这不太合适——我们要的不是幂，而是倍数。

So these are things that look like g + g + ... + g, n times — or, when there are negative multiples, putting in the inverses.
好的，我们开始上课。: 这些是形如 g + g + … + g（n 次）的东西；遇到负倍数时，就把逆元用进去。

So as n ranges over Z, in particular the cyclic subgroup generated by 1-bar contains 1-bar, 1-bar + 1-bar, 1-bar + 1-bar + 1-bar...
好的，我们开始上课。: 当 n 取遍 Z 时，由 1-bar 生成的循环子群特别包含 1-bar, 1-bar + 1-bar, 1-bar + 1-bar + 1-bar, ……

...so it certainly contains 1-bar added to itself k times.
好的，我们开始上课。: ……所以它当然包含 1-bar 自加 k 次的结果。

Well, if I add 1-bar to itself k times, then I get k-bar — because by associativity, 1-bar plus itself k times is just (1 + 1 + ... + 1)-bar, and that is k-bar.
好的，我们开始上课。: 把 1-bar 自加 k 次，就得到 k-bar——因为由结合律，1-bar 自加 k 次就是 (1 + 1 + … + 1)-bar，也就是 k-bar。

So that's k-bar. In particular, in the cyclic subgroup generated by 1-bar I have 1-bar, 2-bar, all the way up to (n − 1)-bar, and n-bar, which is 0.
好的，我们开始上课。: 这就是 k-bar。特别地，由 1-bar 生成的循环子群里含有 1-bar, 2-bar, … 一直到 (n − 1)-bar，以及 n-bar，而 n-bar 就是 0。

But we saw before that's all of the elements — that exhausts all the elements of Z/nZ. So if everything that's in here is in there, these must be equal. Is that clear? Great.
好的，我们开始上课。: 但我们之前看到，这就是全部元素——它穷尽了 Z/nZ 的所有元素。既然这里的元素都在那个子群里，两者必须相等。清楚吗？好。

So, I just — maybe I'll make something I wrote over there even more explicit. Notation: when we use plus for our group operation...
好的，我们开始上课。: 也许我该把那边写的内容再说明确一些。记号约定：当群运算用加号表示时……

...we write n·g — g added to itself n times — not the more multiplicative notation g^n.
好的，我们开始上课。: ……我们写 n·g，也就是 g 自加 n 次；而不是更偏乘法记号的 g^n。

So be careful, because for instance there are certainly two operations that we've defined on Z/nZ; they're different operations and they have different notations.
好的，我们开始上课。: 要小心：我们在 Z/nZ 上定义了两个运算；它们是不同的运算，记号也不同。

Okay, so let's just make a further observation about these two things.
好的，我们开始上课。: 好，我们再看一件关于这两个运算的事情。

Here's a further observation: the addition and multiplication on Z/nZ distribute, in the precise sense that a-bar·(b-bar + c-bar) is the same as a-bar·b-bar + a-bar·c-bar.
好的，我们开始上课。: 再看一个观察：Z/nZ 上的加法和乘法满足分配律，确切地说，a-bar·(b-bar + c-bar) 等于 a-bar·b-bar + a-bar·c-bar。

Now, of course, this seems like an utterly obvious thing, because it's just inheriting what's going on from the integers — this is inherited from Z.
好的，我们开始上课。: 当然，这看起来是显然的，因为它只是从整数继承过来的——它是从 Z 继承的。

And so it's a very, very simple verification. Nonetheless, it's a very important point. It becomes a sort of repeated theme, because we're going to have a lot of things that work very, very similarly to this.
好的，我们开始上课。: 这是一个非常简单的验证，但它非常重要。这也会反复出现，因为后面有很多东西的运作方式与之非常相似。

And this is going to be a major theme when we get to the second part of the course, on ring theory.
好的，我们开始上课。: 等我们讲到课程第二部分——环论时，这会是一个主要主题。

Okay, so here's an example of the usefulness of modular arithmetic.
好的，我们开始上课。: 好，下面看一个例子，说明模算术的用处。

So somebody tell me how to compute the last two digits in the decimal expansion of 2^1000. Go ahead.
好的，我们开始上课。: 谁能告诉我，怎么计算 2^1000 的十进制展开式的最后两位数字？请讲。

Exactly. The answer is: all we have to compute is 2^1000 mod 100, which makes the whole problem extremely manageable.
好的，我们开始上课。: 正是。答案是：我们只需要算 2^1000 mod 100，整个问题就变得非常容易处理。

Completely explicitly — just to show you how easy this is, and also because this is an essential technique used by computers.
好的，我们开始上课。: 我完整地算一遍——既让你们看到这有多容易，也因为这是计算机在用的一项基本技术。

In the case that you need to do things which are analogous to computing the last couple digits in 2^1000, for instance, this is how computers do it.
好的，我们开始上课。: 比如，当你需要做类似计算 2^1000 末几位这种问题时，计算机就是这么做的。

They don't crank out all of 2^1000 — because that's a rather large number — and convert it to decimal notation; that would not be so efficient.
好的，我们开始上课。: 它们不会把 2^1000 整个算出来——那个数相当大——再转成十进制写法；那样效率并不高。

So here's a very simple, short way of computing the thing.
好的，我们开始上课。: 下面是一种非常简单快捷的算法。

Well, 2^10 is 1024, which is congruent to 24 mod 100.
I do this in part because it's just useful — you have to get used to writing things in this kind of notation.
好的，我们开始上课。: 我讲这个，一部分是因为它确实有用——你们得习惯这种记号。

If I square this, so 2^20 — well, that's (2^10)^2...
...and that means this is 24^2 mod 100, which is 576, which is congruent to 76 mod 100.
Are there any questions about the computation so far? Is this clear to everyone?
好的，我们开始上课。: 到目前为止的计算有问题吗？大家都清楚吗？

Now if I square 76, this is 5776, which is just 76 mod 100.
好的，我们开始上课。: 现在把 76 平方，得到 5776，它模 100 就等于 76。

What is 76^n mod 100? 76!
好的，我们开始上课。: 那么 76^n 模 100 是多少？还是 76！

This implies that 76^n is congruent to 76 mod 100, by induction.
好的，我们开始上课。: 用归纳法可知，76^n ≡ 76 (mod 100)。

And so, well — this thing, 2^20, is the 50th root of 2^1000...
...or in other words, 2^1000 equals 2^20 to the 50th power, which is 76^50; so 2^1000 is just congruent to 76 mod 100.
So the question is answered very, very simply.
好的，我们开始上课。: 问题就这样非常简单地解决了。

So far, modular arithmetic has given us one group: Z/nZ with addition.
好的，我们开始上课。: 到这里，模算术给了我们一个群：带加法的 Z/nZ。

With multiplication, is it a group? Somebody — yeah, somebody go ahead.
好的，我们开始上课。: 那么带乘法的 Z/nZ 是群吗？谁来回答——好，请讲。

Right — so this is definitely not a group. No: because for instance 0-bar cannot possibly have an inverse, since anything you multiply it by gives you zero.
好的，我们开始上课。: 对——它绝不是群。因为 0-bar 不可能有逆元：它与任何元素相乘都得到 0。

But can somebody see a subgroup, or can somebody see a subset of Z/nZ which gives a group?
好的，我们开始上课。: 那么谁能看出一个子群，或者 Z/nZ 的一个子集，它能构成一个群？

Go ahead. Exactly — you just do the simplest thing: the problem here is that there are things which don't have inverses, so you just take the ones that have inverses.
好的，我们开始上课。: 请讲。正是——做最简单的事：问题在于有些元素没有逆元，那就把所有有逆元的元素挑出来。

So we define — we do have a subset of Z/nZ which gives a group under multiplication: explicitly, the set of things that have inverses.
好的，我们开始上课。: 我们定义——Z/nZ 中确实有一个子集，在乘法下构成群：就是所有有逆元的元素组成的集合。

So: the a-bar in Z/nZ such that there is c in Z/nZ such that a-bar · c-bar is 1-bar.
好的，我们开始上课。: 即：Z/nZ 中满足"存在 c ∈ Z/nZ，使得 a-bar · c-bar = 1-bar"的所有 a-bar。

And the notation for this thing is (Z/nZ)^×.
好的，我们开始上课。: 这个集合的记号是 (Z/nZ)^×。

This should be a familiar notation to you, because when we talked about the real numbers and the complex numbers, we added a cross to denote the nonzero elements.
好的，我们开始上课。: 这个记号你们应该很熟悉：以前讲实数和复数时，我们在右上角加一个 ×，用来表示非零元素。

Well, those are exactly the elements which have inverses, so this is an entirely consistent notation.
好的，我们开始上课。: 而那些非零元素正好就是有逆元的元素，所以这个记号完全一致。

Okay, so just to make sure that this is entirely clear: well, the associativity again is inherited from the integers.
好的，我们开始上课。: 好，为把这一点完全讲清楚：结合律同样继承自整数。

The identity — well, I've already said what it is — it's 1-bar.
好的，我们开始上课。: 单位元——我已经说过——是 1-bar。

1-bar has a natural inverse, namely itself, so it's certainly in there.
好的，我们开始上课。: 1-bar 有一个自然的逆元，就是它自己，所以它当然在这个集合里。

And the inverses — well, that's by definition; inverses by construction.
好的，我们开始上课。: 至于逆元——按定义就有；逆元是构造出来的。

So let's have a brief recall on gcds, because we're going to want to discover the structure of this thing...
好的，我们开始上课。: 下面简短回顾一下最大公因数，因为我们想弄清这个集合的结构……

...we want to know what this thing looks like, and it turns out that this is tied up with some very, very elementary arithmetic.
好的，我们开始上课。: ……想知道它长什么样；结果这件事跟非常初等的算术联系在一起。

So, to understand (Z/nZ)^×, review of greatest common divisors.
好的，我们开始上课。: 所以，为了理解 (Z/nZ)^×，先回顾最大公因数。

So if I have m and n integers — and I'm going to assume they're not both zero; it's just a hypothesis that's going to make theorems easier to write down.
好的，我们开始上课。: 设 m、n 是整数——我假设它们不全为零；这只是一个让定理写起来更方便的假设。

So what is the gcd? Well, you were probably taught this in elementary school as the largest positive integer...
好的，我们开始上课。: 什么是最大公因数？你们大概在小学就学过：它是最大的正整数……

...where this is a sort of redundant part of the definition — the largest integer that divides both of these things, dividing m and n.
好的，我们开始上课。: ……这里"正"其实是定义中冗余的一部分——也就是能同时整除 m 和 n 的最大整数。

But for the purposes of understanding the gcd, there's of course a better way of writing this down, because it doesn't make reference to the order structure on the integers inherited from the real numbers.
好的，我们开始上课。: 但为了真正理解最大公因数，有一种更好的写法，因为它不涉及整数从实数那里继承来的序结构。

In other words, it doesn't talk about positives and negatives. There's another order structure that is induced by just multiplication — or in other words, the division relationship between things.
好的，我们开始上课。: 换句话说，它不谈正负。还有一种"序"结构只由乘法诱导出来——也就是元素之间的整除关系。

So this is the unique positive integer d such that d divides m and n, and if e divides m and n, then e divides d.
好的，我们开始上课。: 也就是说，它是唯一满足下述条件的正整数 d：d 整除 m 和 n；并且如果 e 也整除 m 和 n，那么 e 整除 d。

And it's very, very easy to verify — of course, you've surely done this in another course — that this number has this property.
好的，我们开始上课。: 很容易验证——你们肯定在别的课上学过——这个数具有上述性质。

Now the major fact — the main fact that I want to prove about gcds — is that they have a relationship to the group structure, or subgroup structure, on Z that we've studied so far. Yes?
好的，我们开始上课。: 接下来是这个主要结论——关于最大公因数我想证明的核心事实：它与我们迄今研究过的 Z 的群结构（子群结构）有关系。有问题吗？

Sorry, what's the question? Oh — the unique positive integer d such that d divides m and n, and if you have another common divisor, then it divides the greatest common divisor; so it's just talking about the division structure of the thing.
好的，我们开始上课。: 抱歉，问题是什么？哦——就是那个唯一正整数 d：它整除 m 和 n，而任何公因数都整除 d；也就是说，它谈的只是整除结构。

So: mZ + nZ. First question: these are both subgroups of Z — is mZ + nZ a subgroup of Z?
好的，我们开始上课。: 那么看 mZ + nZ。第一个问题：它们都是 Z 的子群——mZ + nZ 是 Z 的子群吗？

The answer is yes, and it's not hard to see: 0 is certainly in there; it's certainly closed under addition...
好的，我们开始上课。: 答案是肯定的，而且不难看出：0 当然在其中；它对加法封闭……

...and the negative of something in here is certainly again in here, because these are just things of the form mr + ns, and you just negate those, etc.
好的，我们开始上课。: ……其中元素的负元当然也还在其中，因为这些东西都是形如 mr + ns 的元素，取负即可。

So this is certainly a subgroup. But we know what all the subgroups of Z look like: they look like some number — some positive integer, in fact — times Z.
好的，我们开始上课。: 所以它当然是子群。而我们知道 Z 的所有子群长什么样：它们都形如某个数——其实是某个正整数——乘以 Z。

So any guesses as to what this is? Go ahead.
好的，我们开始上课。: 那么有谁猜一猜这是什么？请讲。

dZ! Exactly. The answer is gcd(m, n)Z. That was a hard one to guess.
好的，我们开始上课。: dZ！正是。答案是 gcd(m, n)Z。这可不好猜。

Proof: well, this is a fairly easy verification, but I'll just go through it very quickly.
好的，我们开始上课。: 证明：这其实是一个相当容易的验证，我快速过一遍。

So as I said, this thing is a subgroup of Z, so it looks like something — so it equals dZ for some d, and we can assume d is a positive integer.
好的，我们开始上课。: 如我所说，它是 Z 的子群，所以它形如某个子群——它等于 dZ（对某个 d），且可以假设 d 是正整数。

Now, since m is in mZ + nZ, which is exactly dZ, d certainly divides m. Same argument: d divides n.
好的，我们开始上课。: 由于 m ∈ mZ + nZ = dZ，所以 d 一定整除 m。同理，d 整除 n。

So the first part of this is verified — the first part of this characterizing property is verified.
好的，我们开始上课。: 这个刻画性质的前一半就验证完毕了。

Second part: well, suppose I have e dividing m and n. Well, because d is in dZ, I can write d as mr + ns.
好的，我们开始上课。: 后一半：假设 e 整除 m 和 n。由于 d 在 dZ 中，我可以把 d 写成 mr + ns。

And if e divides m and e divides n, then e divides mr + ns, and hence e divides d. Is that clear?
好的，我们开始上课。: 而如果 e 整除 m、也整除 n，那么 e 整除 mr + ns，从而 e 整除 d。清楚吗？

So this is exactly the characterizing property: d divides m and n, and if something divides m and n, then it divides d.
好的，我们开始上课。: 这正好就是刻画性质：d 整除 m 和 n；而任何整除 m 和 n 的东西都整除 d。

So we've verified the properties, and we've proved the lemma. There you go.
好的，我们开始上课。: 性质验证完毕，引理也就证好了。就是这样。

Now let's use this fact to prove a proposition.
好的，我们开始上课。: 下面用这个事实来证明一个命题。

Proposition: (Z/nZ)^× is exactly the set of a-bar in Z/nZ such that — any guesses? — yes, exactly: gcd(a, n) = 1.
好的，我们开始上课。: 命题：(Z/nZ)^× 恰好就是 Z/nZ 中满足——有谁猜一下？——对，正是 gcd(a, n) = 1 的那些 a-bar。

Or, to use a more abbreviated terminology: a and n are relatively prime.
好的，我们开始上课。: 或者用一个更简短的词：a 与 n 互素。

Now, this is very easy to prove, now that we've established these basic arithmetic facts about the subgroups of Z.
好的，我们开始上课。: 既然我们已经建立了关于 Z 的子群的这些基本算术事实，这就很容易证明了。

Well, there is one subtle point here. What would be a subtle point in just writing down this set? Yes?
好的，我们开始上课。: 不过这里有一个细微之处。直接写出这个集合，会有什么细微的问题？你请讲。

Well, there's a bit of an issue with writing this down, because you'll notice that on the left part of this I'm taking a-bar in Z/nZ, and on the right part I'm removing the bar.
好的，我们开始上课。: 这么写确实有点问题：你会注意到，左边我写的是 Z/nZ 中的 a-bar，右边我却把横线去掉了。

There's no unique lift: if I have some equivalence class a-bar, there are many, many possible representatives.
好的，我们开始上课。: 并没有唯一的提升：一个等价类 a-bar 有很多很多个可能的代表元。

So there's a slightly subtle point here: namely, that if I have one element of an equivalence class which is relatively prime to n, then every element of that equivalence class is also relatively prime to n.
好的，我们开始上课。: 所以这里有个细微之处：如果等价类中有一个元素与 n 互素，那么这个等价类中的每个元素都与 n 互素。

Now, this isn't difficult to show, but it's certainly a bit of a subtlety in writing down this thing.
好的，我们开始上课。: 这一点不难证明，但确实是写下这个集合时的一个细微之处。

But anyway, I'll go on and prove this proposition.
好的，我们开始上课。: 不管怎样，我接着来证明这个命题。

So, first: the right-hand side is included in the left-hand side.
好的，我们开始上课。: 第一步：右边包含于左边。

Well, if I have gcd(a, n) = 1, then by the lemma — the lemma implies that aZ + nZ = Z.
好的，我们开始上课。: 如果 gcd(a, n) = 1，那么由引理——引理说明 aZ + nZ = Z。

Or put another way — it's equivalent, but it's also just something that follows immediately, because 1 is in there — I can write 1 as ar + ns for some r and s.
好的，我们开始上课。: 换句话说——这两者等价，而且也很直接，因为 1 在里面——我可以把 1 写成 ar + ns，其中 r、s 是整数。

So why is this significant? Well, this tells us that ar − 1 is in nZ...
好的，我们开始上课。: 这为什么重要？因为它告诉我们 ar − 1 ∈ nZ……

...or put another way, a-bar · r-bar = 1-bar. So a-bar is certainly in (Z/nZ)^×.
好的，我们开始上课。: ……换句话说，a-bar · r-bar = 1-bar。所以 a-bar 当然属于 (Z/nZ)^×。

Now the converse is very, very similar: left-hand side contained in right-hand side.
好的，我们开始上课。: 反过来就非常相似：左边包含于右边。

Well, do the same sort of thing: if a-bar · c-bar equals 1-bar, then I can write ac − 1 = nb for some integer b.
好的，我们开始上课。: 做同样的事：如果 a-bar · c-bar = 1-bar，那么可以写成 ac − 1 = nb，其中 b 是整数。

So 1, which is ac minus nb, is in aZ + nZ — but this thing is just gcd(a, n)Z.
好的，我们开始上课。: 于是 1 = ac − nb，属于 aZ + nZ——而这个子群正是 gcd(a, n)Z。
